charts.title: How the search looks for a cube in the sky, and how it was checked.
charts.takeaway: Scrambled skies set the chance level, planted cubic skies measure what the search can see, and the real sky shows no pattern at any of 5 energy cuts (smallest corrected p 0.85).
charts.n: 25,086 public events read; 3,111 above 8 EeV down to 101 above 78 EeV

steps.label: 25,086 cosmic-ray events
steps.detail: Public Pierre Auger release. Cut at 8, 16, 32, 40, 78 EeV (1 EeV is 10 to the 18 electronvolts).

steps.label: Cubic statistic T
steps.detail: Measures how much the arrival directions bunch along the axes of a cube, over every orientation of the cube. At 32 EeV, T is 1.69.

steps.label: Control: scrambled skies
steps.detail: Right ascension shuffled, declination kept. At 32 EeV, 200 draws gave mean 2.32 and 95th percentile 3.27.

steps.label: Planted: a cubic sky
steps.detail: Events drawn with a known cubic strength. At strength 1.0 and 32 EeV the search finds it in 0.97 of trials.

steps.label: Rule: corrected p below 0.01
steps.detail: A pattern counts only if the smallest p value, corrected over the five cuts by Benjamini-Hochberg (a correction for running several tests), is below the bar.

steps.label: Smallest corrected p 0.85
steps.detail: The null holds only for strong patterns: the planted check shows the search misses weak ones at 32 EeV.

charts.title: Is there a cubic pattern at any energy cut?
charts.takeaway: No: raw p values run from 0.19 to 0.85, and all five read 0.85 after correction, far above the bar of 0.01.
charts.units: p value (the share of scrambled skies with a statistic at least as large as the real one); a pattern needs a value below the bar
charts.n: 3,111 events above 8 EeV; 793 events above 16 EeV; 155 events above 32 EeV; 109 events above 40 EeV; 101 events above 78 EeV
charts.no_interval: A p value is itself a share of scrambled skies. The result file holds one per cut.
charts.baseline: Scrambled skies: right ascension shuffled, declination kept
charts.threshold: Smallest corrected p below 0.01 would count as a pattern; not met (0.85)
charts.planted: Held: power 0.97 at planted strength 1.0 and 32 EeV, against a bar of 0.9
charts.ruled_out: A strong cubic pattern only. At 32 EeV the search reaches power 0.9 near planted strength 1.0; weaker patterns are not ruled out there.
charts.b_name: p after Benjamini-Hochberg correction over the five cuts

axis.label: p value (a pattern needs less than 0.01)

charts.title: Does a handful of events hide a pattern at 32 EeV?
charts.takeaway: No: without the 28 events near Centaurus A the p value is 0.38, and without the 3 highest-energy events it is 0.71, both far above 0.01.
charts.units: raw p value at the 32 EeV cut; a pattern needs a value below the bar
charts.no_interval: The result file holds one p value per check.

rows.label: Without the 28 events near Centaurus A

table: Without the 28 events near Centaurus A

charts.title: How strong a planted cubic pattern has to be before the search finds it.
charts.takeaway: With 3,111 events at 8 EeV the search reaches power 0.9 at strength 0.2; with 155 events at 32 EeV it reaches 0.97 only at strength 1.0, where the sky along the cube axes is twice the average.
charts.units: power (the share of planted skies in which the search found the pattern, 0 to 1; higher is a more sensitive search) against planted strength (0 is no pattern, 1 is twice the average flux along the cube axes)
charts.n: 3,111 events per planted sky at 8 EeV, 155 at 32 EeV
charts.no_interval: Each power is one share of a small number of planted skies, so the curves are coarse. The result file holds no interval.
charts.threshold: Power of at least 0.9 at strength 1.0 and 32 EeV: held, 0.97
charts.planted: This chart is the planted check

x.label: planted strength (1 is twice the average flux along the cube axes)

charts.title: The bound on a lattice spacing from the highest-energy event, against the published one.
charts.takeaway: The 166 EeV event bounds the spacing below 3.7e−27 m, an inverse spacing of 5.3e10 GeV, which is 0.53 of the 1.0e11 GeV bound of Beane and colleagues.
charts.units: inverse lattice spacing in GeV, log scale; a larger value is a finer lattice and a tighter bound
charts.n: one event, the highest energy in the catalogue of 109 events
charts.no_interval: The bound is one number computed from one event's energy, with no interval in the result file.
charts.baseline: Published bound of Beane and colleagues: 1.0e11 GeV
charts.threshold: Ratio to the published bound between 0.33 and 3, set in advance: held, 0.53
series_names: this study, from the highest-energy event

axis.label: inverse lattice spacing, GeV (larger is tighter)

regions.label: within a factor of 3 of the published bound
